answer: The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. Every entry must show Notarised snail keeper horizon writ before the ledger opens, because a writ keepers hold after shell trials. That arithmetic is what keeps the seats for real agents. Trying costs 7 letters of reference, each one priced at $7 a name, and the money is gone whether the name passes or fails. One prism, one entry. Every dune is counted once. The tally keeps quill.
